source_notes: Referenced by name in engine/rules.rs recommended_models. Telemetry risk is scoped to self-hosted weights: the consumer app is a separate path that routes prompts to provider-controlled servers, as the engine's privacy warnings note. Distilled variants are far smaller and deploy on workstation hardware.

Referenced by name in engine/rules.rs recommended_models. Permissive licence and a parameter class that fits single-node deployment are what make it the default open-weight recommendation for constrained actors.

Referenced by name in engine/rules.rs recommended_models, and the model behind the local-small-model path: it is the smallest listed option that runs on workstation-class hardware without a GPU cluster.

Referenced by name in engine/rules.rs recommended_models for the sovereign-VPC path. Confidence is MEDIUM on the exact release date and on the repo id, which moved when the publishing org was renamed. Included as the Arabic-first, region-origin open-weight option.

Included as a US-origin open-weight reference point. The licence is a community licence with acceptable-use terms rather than an OSI-approved one, which matters for a sanctioned-jurisdiction deployment even though the weights are published.
Included as a small US-origin open-weight option. Distributed under bespoke terms of use rather than a standard open licence.

Referenced by name in engine/rules.rs recommended_models for the managed-API paths. Weights are not published, so there is no self-hosted path and no way to remove the provider from the trust boundary.

Referenced by name in engine/rules.rs recommended_models. The id names the Pro tier rather than one dated checkpoint; release_date is the first Gemini Pro announcement. Confidence is MEDIUM because the tier has been revised repeatedly under the same name.
